papers.title: Multi-view Learning as a Nonparametric Nonlinear Inter-Battery Factor Analysis
papers.abstract: Factor analysis aims to determine latent factors, or traits, which summarize a given data set. Inter-battery factor analysis extends this notion to multiple views of the data. In this paper we show how a nonlinear, nonparametric version of these models can be recovered through the Gaussian process latent variable model. This gives us a flexible formalism for multi-view learning where the latent variables can be used both for exploratory purposes and for learning representations that enable efficient inference for ambiguous estimation tasks. Learning is performed in a Bayesian manner through the formulation of a variational compression scheme which gives a rigorous lower bound on the log likelihood. Our Bayesian framework provides strong regularization during training, allowing the structure of the latent space to be determined efficiently and automatically. We demonstrate this by producing the first (to our knowledge) published results of learning from dozens of views, even when data is scarce. We further show experimental results on several different types of multi-view data sets and for different kinds of tasks, including exploratory data analysis, generation, ambiguity modelling through latent priors and classification.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文提出了一种多视图学习的非参数非线性因子分析方法，但与有限元代理建模或生物力学设计无直接关联。

summary_zh.motivation: 提出一种非参数非线性多视图因子分析方法，用于探索性分析和表示学习。
summary_zh.method: 通过高斯过程潜变量模型扩展互电池因子分析，并采用变分压缩方案进行贝叶斯学习。
summary_zh.result: 在多个多视图数据集上展示了探索性分析、生成和分类任务的有效性。
summary_zh.validation: 在多个多视图数据集上进行实验验证，包括分类和生成任务。

summary_en.motivation: To develop a nonlinear nonparametric multi-view factor analysis method for exploratory analysis and representation learning.
summary_en.method: Extends inter-battery factor analysis using Gaussian process latent variable models with a variational compression scheme for Bayesian learning.
summary_en.result: Demonstrates effectiveness on multiple multi-view datasets for exploratory analysis, generation, and classification tasks.
summary_en.validation: Validated on several multi-view datasets with tasks including classification and generation.

papers.title: Regularizing Solutions to the MEG Inverse Problem Using Space-Time Separable Covariance Functions
papers.abstract: In magnetoencephalography (MEG) the conventional approach to source reconstruction is to solve the underdetermined inverse problem independently over time and space. Here we present how the conventional approach can be extended by regularizing the solution in space and time by a Gaussian process (Gaussian random field) model. Assuming a separable covariance function in space and time, the computational complexity of the proposed model becomes (without any further assumptions or restrictions) $\mathcal{O}(t^3 + n^3 + m^2n)$, where $t$ is the number of time steps, $m$ is the number of sources, and $n$ is the number of sensors. We apply the method to both simulated and empirical data, and demonstrate the efficiency and generality of our Bayesian source reconstruction approach which subsumes various classical approaches in the literature.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究脑磁图逆问题，与用户关注的有限元替代建模和生物力学设计无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper applies Gaussian process regularization to a neuroscience inverse problem (MEG), with no connection to FEA surrogate modeling, implant design, or biomechanics constraints.

summary_zh.motivation: 解决脑磁图逆问题的时空正则化。
summary_zh.method: 使用时空可分离协方差函数的高斯过程模型进行贝叶斯源重建。
summary_zh.result: 计算方法复杂度降低，适用于模拟和实测数据。
summary_zh.validation: 通过模拟数据和真实脑磁图数据验证。

summary_en.motivation: To regularize the ill-posed MEG inverse problem by incorporating spatiotemporal smoothness constraints.
summary_en.method: A Gaussian process (Gaussian random field) model with a separable space-time covariance function is proposed for Bayesian source reconstruction.
summary_en.result: The method achieves computational complexity O(t^3 + n^3 + m^2 n) and successfully recovers sources from simulated and empirical MEG data.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed on both simulated datasets and empirical MEG recordings, demonstrating performance comparable to classical approaches.
